Byomkesh.description: A renowned detective and truth-seeker who investigates mysteries with keen observation and logic.

Ajit.description: The narrator and chronicler of Byomkesh's adventures, he is Byomkesh's close friend and often assists in investigations.

Bhupesh Chatterjee.description: A middle-aged, refined insurance company employee and recent resident of the boarding house, who is deeply fond of bridge.

Satyabati.description: Byomkesh's wife, who manages the household and shares a warm relationship with her husband.

Ramchandra Roy.description: A grave and taciturn bank employee, later revealed to be Rashbehari Biswas.

Banamali Chanda.description: A reticent bank employee with an Eastern Bengali accent, later revealed to be Banabehari Biswas.

Natabar Nashkar.description: A solitary boarder on the ground floor, later revealed to have been a blackmailer, whose murder is central to the story.

Shibkali Chakraborty.description: The manager of the boarding house, a bachelor who has run the establishment for twenty-five years.

Pranab Guha.description: The local police inspector, competent but not fond of Byomkesh, who investigates Natabar Nashkar's murder.

Haripada.description: The servant in the boarding house, who provides a potentially significant observation about Natabar's last visitor.

Suren-babu.description: A first-floor resident who sends Haripada to buy snacks and provides a time reference for the investigation.

Swami Pranabananda.description: Mentioned as someone Byomkesh suggests visiting, though not directly involved in the main plot.

Cuttack.description: A city in Odisha, India, where Byomkesh and Ajit travel for official work.

Calcutta.description: Now known as Kolkata, a major city in West Bengal, India, and the primary setting of the story.

Dhaka.description: The capital of Bangladesh, referenced as the former home of several characters before the Partition.

Partition.description: Refers to the 1947 division of British India into India and Pakistan, causing mass migrations and communal violence.

Godfrey-Brown.description: A large British firm with offices in Dhaka and Calcutta, where Ram-babu and Banamali-babu formerly worked.

West Bengal.description: An Indian state, referenced as the destination for refugees from Dhaka after the Partition.

Rabindranath Tagore.description: A renowned Bengali poet and Nobel laureate, quoted by Bhupesh-babu.

Sarat Chandra Chattopadhyay.description: A famous Bengali novelist, referenced by Byomkesh in the conclusion.

Marwari store.description: A shop run by members of the Marwari community, known for their business acumen, from which snacks are bought.

American army pistol.description: A type of firearm mentioned as the murder weapon, available on the black market.

Commissioner.description: Refers to the police commissioner, the senior-most police official in the city.

babu.description: A respectful suffix or form of address for men in Bengali and other Indian languages, similar to 'Mr.'

churidar.description: A type of close-fitting trousers worn in South Asia, often paired with a kurta or jacket.

dhoti.description: A traditional Indian garment for men, consisting of a long piece of cloth wrapped around the waist and legs.

addicted to bridge.description: Refers to a strong fondness for the card game bridge, which is culturally popular among some Indian communities.

kayastha.description: A Hindu caste traditionally associated with scribes and administrators in Bengal and other parts of India.

vaidya.description: A traditional practitioner of Ayurvedic medicine, also a caste in Bengal.

anna.description: A former Indian currency unit, equal to 1/16 of a rupee, used before decimalization.

shawl.description: A large piece of fabric worn over the shoulders or head, commonly used in Indian attire, especially in winter.

sari.description: A traditional garment worn by women in India, consisting of a long piece of cloth draped around the body.

rubber.description: In the context of card games, a set of games (usually three) that determines the overall winner.

passbook.description: A small book used to record banking transactions, commonly used in India.

godown.description: A warehouse or storage facility, a term commonly used in India and Southeast Asia.
